newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end up after stock plunge.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end up after stock plunge.

text.p: Key September Euroyen futures ended Friday's TIFFE day session higher following a rise in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures and a nosedive in Tokyo stocks.
The September closed up 0.03 at 99.33, after trading between 99.28 and 99.33. Volume was 53,543 contracts.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended down 770.22 points, or 4.26 percent, at 17,303.65.
"Euroyen futures tested higher levels following the rise in JGB futures and the Nikkei's plunge," a city bank trader said.
The key March JGB futures contract ended 0.42 higher at 125.37.
Traders said the weakness in Tokyo stocks was supportive for Euroyen futures as it underscored the market's view that Japan's short-term interest rates would remain stable at a low level.
Some traders said that further weakness in stock prices could lead to speculation that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would allow short-term interest rates to fall.

However, a trader at another city bank said: "It is doubtful that the BOJ will guide short-term rates lower as the impact of such a measure on stocks should be limited. Moreover, it might trigger further weakness in the yen."
Traders said that while Euroyen futures were seen remaining firm, the upside may be limited.
"Although the September may edge higher in coming sessions, there isn't that much room left for further rise," the second trader said.
The key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.46 percent, down from 0.48 percent on Thursday.
The BOJ injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market in the morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
The overnight call rate eased due to weaker fund demand ahead of the weekend, traders said.
A hefty 315 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.53 percent.
About 100 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.51 percent and about 30 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.50 percent. All CD rates were unchanged from Thursday.
